name: Taylor Chan
life: “I still remember canceling a subscription for a newly admitted patient.” People around Tideline Market know Taylor by a small Thursday habit. Taylor picks out the bruised fruit first and asks the seller what will ripen by supper.
voice: I suggested a subscription. The residents asked what happens to the fee when they go into hospital.
appearance: Taylor has a strong profile and a little space between the front teeth. Look for dark brown curls cut close behind the ears. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a cropped bottle-green coat with a replacement button a shade darker than the others. In conversation Taylor presses the lips together to keep a smile in.
personality: Taylor is firm about boundaries and unusually forgiving of somebody who admits to crossing one. Demands to act grateful for unwanted help can end a friendship.
agenda: To pause fees when a subscriber enters hospital.
family: Leon Cole is Taylor’s second cousin. Taylor sets the time to leave. Leon picks the meeting place. It lets them stay close without turning a family visit into the loss of an entire day. They have both had stretches when that distinction mattered. Asked about *A chair of one's own*, Leon says, “I own the studio. I called the offer independence before asking who buys the empty hours.”
connections: Roman Sutton. The investor and bookkeeper agree on what happens to a fee during a hospital stay.

reactions.situation: A housebound customer cannot afford the delivery fee
reactions.response: Taylor asks whether combining a delivery with a willing neighbor would help.

reactions.situation: A stranger waves a phone camera in a crying person's face
reactions.response: Taylor asks the filmer to lower the phone and gets another familiar face to stand by the person crying.

reactions.situation: If a relative arrives with a solution nobody requested
reactions.response: Taylor thanks them for coming and explains the part that still belongs to the household.
